info.title: QuickStack REST API
info.description: This is the REST API for QuickStack. Furhter details about QuickStack can be found in the [documentation](https://quickstack.dev).

tags.name: Apps
tags.description: CRUD, deploy and monitoring operations for app workloads.

tags.name: Agents
tags.description: CRUD and deploy operations for agent templates. Agent templates are a definition of a structure of an agent. Running agents are called "Agent Sandboxes".

tags.name: Agent Sandboxes
tags.description: Start/Stop operations for agent sandboxes (running instances of an agent) and APIs to interact with running agent sandbox instances.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of projects. The default limit is 50.

schema.description: Maximum number of items to return (1-100, default 50).
Opaque continuation cursor from a previous response. Send it together with limit.

post.description: Creates a project when id is omitted, otherwise updates the existing project. Requires admin.

delete.description: Permanently deletes the project, all its Apps and Agents, and the Kubernetes namespace with their workloads and volumes. Requires admin.
delete.x-mcp-description:
Permanently deletes the project, all its Apps and Agents, and the Kubernetes namespace with their workloads and volumes. No request body.
Requires admin and confirmation because this cannot be undone.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of apps. The default limit is 50.

schema.description: Maximum number of items to return (1-100, default 50).
Opaque continuation cursor from a previous response. Send it together with limit.

post.description: Creates an app when id is omitted, otherwise replaces the existing app. projectId cannot be changed. Call deployApp afterwards to roll out the desired state.
post.x-mcp-description:
Upsert one App.
- Omit id to create: projectId is required. appDomains, appNodePorts, appFileMounts, appVolumes and appBasicAuths are required arrays (empty allowed), and appNetworkPolicy must be null or an object.
- Send id to update: projectId must equal the existing app's projectId and cannot be changed. The request replaces the stored app, so omitted or empty sub-resource arrays delete the existing entries. Call getApp first, then send the full object back with the ids of sub-resources you want to keep.
- When MCP secret redaction is enabled, getApp omits envVars, buildArgs, gitToken, containerRegistryPassword and appBasicAuths[].password. Obtain the existing values from a secure source and include them when updating; do not substitute empty strings, which can overwrite secrets. If the values are unavailable, do not update the app.
- This only saves desired state. Call deployApp afterwards to roll it out. Saving revalidates server caches but does not change Kubernetes resources.

Example create:
{"name":"web","appType":"APP","projectId":"<projectId>","sourceType":"CONTAINER","buildMethod":"RAILPACK","containerImageSource":"nginx:1.27","dockerfilePath":"./Dockerfile","replicas":1,"envVars":"","buildArgs":"","useNetworkPolicy":true,"healthCheckPeriodSeconds":15,"healthCheckTimeoutSeconds":5,"healthCheckFailureThreshold":3,"appDomains":[{"hostname":"web.example.com","port":80,"useSsl":true,"redirectHttps":true}],"appNodePorts":[],"appFileMounts":[],"appVolumes":[],"appBasicAuths":[],"appNetworkPolicy":null}

Example update (read getApp first and keep all sub-resource ids you do not want to delete):
{"id":"<appId>","name":"web","appType":"APP","projectId":"<projectId>","sourceType":"CONTAINER","buildMethod":"DOCKERFILE","containerImageSource":"nginx:1.27","dockerfilePath":"./Dockerfile","replicas":2,"envVars":"<existing envVars>","buildArgs":"<existing buildArgs>","useNetworkPolicy":true,"healthCheckPeriodSeconds":15,"healthCheckTimeoutSeconds":5,"healthCheckFailureThreshold":3,"appDomains":[{"id":"<domainId>","hostname":"web.example.com","port":80,"useSsl":true,"redirectHttps":true}],"appNodePorts":[],"appFileMounts":[],"appVolumes":[],"appBasicAuths":[],"appNetworkPolicy":null}

get.description: Returns the current log tail of the app. `lines` defaults to 200 and is limited to 5000.
get.x-mcp-description: Returns the current log tail of the app. Keep `lines` small (default 200, max 5000); large responses are truncated by MCP clients.

post.description: Runs a shell command in the first running Pod of the app. Returns stdout, stderr and exitCode.

delete.description: Permanently deletes the app and its sub-resources (domains, volumes, file mounts, basic auth).
delete.x-mcp-description:
Permanently deletes the app and its sub-resources (domains, volumes, file mounts, basic auth). No request body.
Requires confirmation because this cannot be undone.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of agents. The default limit is 50.

schema.description: Maximum number of items to return (1-100, default 50).
Opaque continuation cursor from a previous response. Send it together with limit.

post.description: Creates an agent template when id is omitted, otherwise replaces the existing template. projectId cannot be changed. Call deployAgent afterwards to apply it.
post.x-mcp-description:
Upsert one agent template.
- Omit id to create: projectId, llmGatewayId and modelAlias (non-empty array) are required. agentDomains, agentVolumes, agentFileMounts are required arrays, and agentNetworkPolicy must be null or an object.
- Send id to update: projectId must equal the existing agent's projectId and cannot be changed. The request replaces the stored agent, so omitted or empty sub-resource arrays delete the existing entries. Call getAgent first, then send the full object back with the ids of sub-resources you want to keep.
- When MCP secret redaction is enabled, getAgent omits gitToken and containerRegistryPassword. Obtain existing values from a secure source and include them when updating; do not substitute empty strings, which can overwrite secrets. If the values are unavailable, do not update the agent.
- This only saves the template. Call deployAgent to apply it, then startAgentSandbox to run a sandbox. Saving revalidates caches but does not create Kubernetes resources.

Example create:
{"name":"coder","projectId":"<projectId>","llmGatewayId":"<gatewayId>","modelAlias":["gpt-4o"],"sourceType":"CONTAINER","buildMethod":"DOCKERFILE","containerImageSource":"ghcr.io/example/agent:latest","dockerfilePath":"./Dockerfile","warmPoolReplicas":0,"deployFileBrowser":false,"healthCheckPeriodSeconds":15,"healthCheckTimeoutSeconds":5,"healthCheckFailureThreshold":3,"agentDomains":[],"agentVolumes":[],"agentFileMounts":[],"agentNetworkPolicy":null}

Example update (read getAgent first and keep all sub-resource ids you do not want to delete):
{"id":"<agentId>","name":"coder","projectId":"<projectId>","llmGatewayId":"<gatewayId>","modelAlias":["gpt-4o","gpt-4o-mini"],"sourceType":"CONTAINER","buildMethod":"DOCKERFILE","containerImageSource":"ghcr.io/example/agent:latest","dockerfilePath":"./Dockerfile","warmPoolReplicas":1,"deployFileBrowser":false,"healthCheckPeriodSeconds":15,"healthCheckTimeoutSeconds":5,"healthCheckFailureThreshold":3,"agentDomains":[],"agentVolumes":[{"id":"<volumeId>","containerMountPath":"/workspace","size":10,"storageClassName":"longhorn","volumeType":"PER_SANDBOX"}],"agentFileMounts":[],"agentNetworkPolicy":{"allowInternetAccess":true,"rules":[]}}

delete.description: Permanently deletes the agent template and its sub-resources (domains, volumes, file mounts, network policy).
delete.x-mcp-description:
Permanently deletes the agent template and its sub-resources (domains, volumes, file mounts, network policy). No request body.
Requires confirmation because this cannot be undone.

post.description: Deploys the agent configuration to Kubernetes as a SandboxTemplate. Does not start a sandbox. Can only be done when no sandbox is running.
post.x-mcp-description:
Deploys the agent configuration with the given ID. This does not start any agent sandbox; it only applies the configuration to Kubernetes (SandboxTemplate). Every new agent sandbox created after this deployment uses the newly applied configuration. This can only be done when no sandbox is running. For CONTAINER sources the SandboxTemplate is applied before the call returns. For GIT/GIT_SSH sources the build continues asynchronously after the returned deploymentId; follow its progress in the QuickStack UI and poll listAgentSandboxes before starting a sandbox.
This changes live Kubernetes resources; ask for confirmation first.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of running agent sandboxes. The default limit is 50.

schema.description: Maximum number of items to return (1-100, default 50).
Opaque continuation cursor from a previous response. Send it together with limit.

post.description: Creates and starts one agent sandbox for this agent. The body is optional and defaults to {}. Changes live Kubernetes resources.
post.x-mcp-description:
Creates and starts one agent sandbox for this agent. Body is optional and defaults to {}.
customTag must be 1-63 characters; idleTimeoutMinutes is 1-1440; env names must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*. Query timeoutMs (max 900000, default 300000) controls how long the API waits for the sandbox to start. This creates live Kubernetes resources; ask for confirmation first.

post.summary: Resume agent sandbox by Custom Tag
post.description: Resumes the suspended Agent Sandbox of this Agent that carries the given Custom Tag.
post.x-mcp-description: Resume the suspended Agent Sandbox of this Agent that carries the given Custom Tag. Recreates the Pod with the existing volumes mounted.

post.description: Releases the compute of a running Agent Sandbox while keeping its volumes and identity. The sandbox Pod is deleted and can be resumed later.
post.x-mcp-description: Release the compute of a running Agent Sandbox while keeping its volumes and identity. No request body. The sandbox Pod is deleted and can be resumed later.

post.description: Recreates the Pod of a suspended Agent Sandbox with its existing volumes mounted.
post.x-mcp-description: Recreate the Pod of a suspended Agent Sandbox with its existing volumes mounted. No request body.

delete.description: Permanently deletes the agent sandbox and stops its Pod.
delete.x-mcp-description:
Permanently deletes the agent sandbox and stops its Pod. No request body.
Requires confirmation because the running sandbox cannot be recovered.

get.description:
Get a temporary access URL to access the agent sandbox via the browser. This is only possible if a domain is configured for the agent and the agent serves an API or Web interface. No request body; the returned URL expires.
Example: GET /api/v1/agents/<agentId>/sandboxes/<sandboxName>/accessUrl/<domainId>.
get.x-mcp-description: Get a temporary browser access URL for the agent sandbox. The agent must have a configured domain and serve an API or web interface. The URL expires.

post.description:
Create a bearer token for direct API access to this Agent Sandbox through a configured domain. No request body. The token expires after 15 minutes.
Example: POST /api/v1/agents/<agentId>/sandboxes/<sandboxName>/apiToken/<domainId>.
post.x-mcp-description: Create a bearer token for direct API access to the agent sandbox through a configured domain. The token expires after 15 minutes.

delete.description: Deletes all stored data of one Custom Tag across the Agent's PER_CUSTOM_TAG volumes. Rejected while a sandbox with that tag exists.
delete.x-mcp-description:
Delete all stored data of one Custom Tag across the Agent's PER_CUSTOM_TAG volumes. Rejected while a sandbox with that tag exists. No request body.
Requires confirmation because this cannot be undone.

post.description: Runs a shell command in a running Agent Sandbox. timeoutSec is 1-3600 (default 120). Returns stdout, stderr and exitCode.
post.x-mcp-description:
Run a shell command in a running Agent Sandbox. CLI harness templates stay alive with `sleep infinity`; invoke their documented launcher or bootstrap script here so it receives the Agent Runtime Secret and selected LiteLLM Model Alias.
timeoutSec is 1-3600 (default 120). Returns stdout, stderr and exitCode. Requires confirmation because the command can modify sandbox state.

get.description: Stream a file from an agent sandbox. Requires write access to the agent.

put.description:
Writes one file into the running sandbox. Existing content at `path` is replaced.

Use `multipart/form-data` and provide the upload in the required `file` field. This is the supported contract for generated OpenAPI clients.

`swagger-typescript-api` example:

```ts
await client.writeAgentSandboxFile(
  { agentId, sandboxName, path: '/workspace/document.pdf' },
  { file }, // Browser File or Blob
);
```

Do not JSON-serialize the file and do not wrap it in a `body` field. JSON serialization of an `ArrayBuffer` produces `{}` and writes that text to the sandbox file.

Two request formats are supported:

- `multipart/form-data`: required `file` field; preferred for generated OpenAPI clients.
- `application/octet-stream`: request body contains raw file bytes; preferred for direct or streaming HTTP clients.
put.x-mcp-description: Write a file to the running sandbox, replacing any existing content at the specified path.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of files in an agent sandbox. The default limit is 50. Requires write access to the agent.

schema.description: Maximum number of items to return (1-100, default 50).
Opaque continuation cursor from a previous response. Send it together with limit.

get.summary: Check file exists in agent sandbox
get.description: Check a file in an agent sandbox. Requires write access to the agent.
Returns a paginated deployment history. The default limit is 50.
get.x-mcp-description: Returns a paginated deployment history. The default limit is 50. Poll this after deployApp until the newest entry reports success or failure.

schema.description: Maximum number of items to return (1-100, default 50).
Opaque continuation cursor from a previous response. Send it together with limit.

post.description: Starts a build and rollout and returns the deploymentId immediately. Pass forceRebuild=true to rebuild even when the commit/image did not change. This changes live Kubernetes workloads.
post.x-mcp-description:
Starts a build and rollout and returns {"deploymentId":"..."} immediately. Pass query.forceRebuild=true to rebuild even when the commit/image did not change.
Poll listAppDeployments or getAppDeployment with that deploymentId until the status is successful or failed. On failure, call getAppDeploymentLogs to inspect the build logs. This changes live Kubernetes workloads; ask for confirmation first.

get.description: Returns build/deploy logs for one deployment. tailLines is limited to 5000.
get.x-mcp-description: Returns build/deploy logs for one deployment. Keep tailLines small (max 5000); large responses are truncated by MCP clients.
